Prevention: Plant using certified seeds or clean seedlings from reliable nurseries.
Use sterile well-drained soil, cocopeat or peatmoss media.
Plant seeds in soil treated by solarization or fumigation.
Burn dry trash on a wet seedbed to sterilise it.
Raise nursery beds at least 1m above ground level to improve drainage.
Mix topsoil with a thin coating of sand and gravel to improve drainage.
Avoid crowding of seedlings to ensure air circulation.
Don't overwater seedlings or leave them standing in water.
Avoid working with the plants when the soil is too wet.
Avoid planting in previously affected areas.
Sterilize pots, trays, and tools for 30mins by soaking in 1% sodium hypochlorite.
Monitoring: Look for symptoms daily during first 3 weeks after sowing.
Sunken necrotic lesion girdling of the stem near the soil line, eventually leading to the collapse and death of the plant.
Look for emerged seedlings that are severely stunted and do not recover.
Fuzzy white substance on the surface of the damp soil.
Take action after one to three seedlings are affected.
Direct Control: Remove and bury any infected seedlings immediately.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing.
Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, and restricted re- entry intervals.
Always consult a recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Unlikely to present acute hazard (WHO Class
